narration_lines: A city is full of hard surfaces. Roofs and roads cannot drink rain, so the water must be carried.
Under the streets, drains and pipes catch the water and lead it away.
Canals are wide water roads in the city. They carry the water toward the river.
Floodgates open to let water out. Floodgates close when the river is higher than the canal.
When gates close, pumps push the canal's water up into the river.
Deep under the city, big drainage tunnels carry water fast to the river.
Parks and ponds can hold water like a monkey holds food in its cheeks. In Thailand, this is called the Monkey Cheek scheme.
Drains, canals, gates, pumps, tunnels and ponds work as one drainage system. They give the water a way out, or a place to wait.
Across the city, water keeps moving.
